name: MKOS Ontology
source_attribution: MKOS V3 Canonical Architecture Specification + Knowledge Currency Principle + Universal Confidence, Uncertainty and Trust Model (Medical Training App Push, week of 10/17/2026)

change_log.summary: Initial ontology from the MKOS V3 specification.

purpose: Transform medicine from documents into structured knowledge, structured knowledge into educational assets, educational assets into adaptive learning experiences, and adaptive learning experiences into measurable competency growth.

primary_domains.name: Knowledge Domain
primary_domains.purpose: Represent medicine as structured computable knowledge.

primary_domains.name: Educational Domain
primary_domains.purpose: Transform structured knowledge into reusable teaching assets.

primary_domains.name: Learner Intelligence Domain
primary_domains.purpose: Maintain a continuously evolving digital twin of the learner.

primary_domains.name: Governance and Delivery Domain
primary_domains.purpose: Ensure trustworthiness, safety, currency, auditability, and scalability.

layers.name: Adaptive Learning Layer
layers.store: derived from learner state + curriculum (no own store)

object_types.table: mk_objects (+ mk_files for Drive change detection)

structural_relationships.name: derived_from
structural_relationships.basis: Provenance Model: object derived from a Source/Asset

structural_relationships.name: edition_of
structural_relationships.basis: Supersession Model: a Source edition belongs to a Guideline family

structural_relationships.name: teaches
structural_relationships.basis: Asset Generation Model: Educational Asset teaches Concept/Objective

structural_relationships.name: in_specialty
structural_relationships.basis: Knowledge Granularity Model: Specialty > Domain > Competency > Concept

structural_relationships.name: prerequisite_of
structural_relationships.basis: Adaptive Curriculum Model: What To Teach / Delay

facet_model.note: Every concept contains structured facets. A facet value is a list of facet items; each item is Value + Confidence + Provenance + Version + Timestamp (Universal Confidence Model core principle).

levels.name: A
levels.meaning: High-quality evidence from more than one RCT, meta-analyses of high-quality RCTs, or RCTs corroborated by registry studies

levels.name: B-R
levels.meaning: Moderate-quality evidence from one or more RCTs or meta-analyses of moderate-quality RCTs

levels.name: B-NR
levels.meaning: Moderate-quality evidence from well-designed nonrandomized, observational or registry studies

levels.name: C-LD
levels.meaning: Limited data: randomized or nonrandomized studies with limitations of design or execution

levels.name: C-EO
levels.meaning: Consensus of expert opinion based on clinical experience

evidence_model.crosswalk_note: Other grading systems found in sources are normalized onto these five levels (see scoring.json evidence_crosswalk); the original grade is always kept as stated.

provenance_model.rule: Every fact must trace to origin.

routing_model.rule: Always use the lowest-cost authoritative source capable of solving the problem.

ai_governance.implementation: AI-extracted knowledge enters with governance_status 'pending_validation' and an ai_extraction provenance step; its confidence is capped (scoring.json ai_extraction_cap) until validated against the source.

knowledge_currency.historical_override: Historical content is returned only when the request asks for it (include_history=true).
